A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProofBridge work, with matching methods, datasets, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-modal retrieval and proof auto-formalization experiments in Tables 1–2, including ProofBridge component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, domain-level results in Figure 3, and generated outputs in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same modality-specific encoders, proof-state mean pooling, 512-dimensional joint space, contrastive and cross-entropy objectives, retrieval-augmented fine-tuning, and five-attempt repair loop. Newly disclosed hyperparameters and worked examples do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 38,951 NUMINAMATH-LEAN-PF pairs and 244 MINIF2F-TEST-PF problems for the same retrieval and NL-to-Lean formalization tasks. V2's domain breakdown and illustrative example analyze existing coverage; they do not introduce another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds Qwen3-Embedding-8B and E5-Mistral-7B-Instruct to Table 1. Table 2 adds Kimina-Prover-Distill-8B, Kimina-Prover-72B, text-retrieval-assisted Kimina comparisons, and a Herald-Translator → Kimina-Prover-Distill-8B pipeline. These substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives. The original all-MiniLM comparator remains, relabeled as a baseline.

E3.justification: V1 Section 5.2 specifies three-example few-shot evaluation; v2 Section 5.4 specifies five random examples. V2 also introduces Qwen-based retrieval prompting, a two-step sampling and theorem-selection protocol, and the mMG retrieval metric. These materially expand the evaluation design. Retained scores do not establish that experiments were rerun; domain stratification and previously unspecified training settings are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained SFT/retrieval/repair ablations, v2 compares zero-shot, random-example, and retrieved-example conditioning across three Kimina variants. Figure 3 adds domain-level error breakdowns. Appendix A.4 adds a worked comparison of an SC-rejected baseline output and an SC-accepted ProofBridge output, including retrieved demonstrations. These substantially extend analysis of context selection and semantic fidelity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-training variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Retrieval similarity quartiles and pass@k reporting are retained. The new mMG metric and decoding settings do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Previously tabulated numbers are retained, including ProofBridge's 62.70% SC and 95.49% TC at pass@32. V2 adds substantial results: Qwen3 and E5 achieve NL→FL Recall@1 of 46.75% and 35.60%, and the two-step pipeline achieves 43.44% SC and 59.43% TC. Larger-prover, prompting, mMG, domain, and case results are also new. These are added comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains. V2's 72B zero-shot SC is 43.03% in Table 2, contradicting Section 5.5's 46.31%.

T1.justification: The principal mathematical formulation and objectives remain unchanged. V2 defines mMG, revises branch placement in the existing Prop1 ↔ Prop2 Lean proof, and adds an explicit equivalence derivation in Appendix A.4. These are limited mathematical additions and corrections, without a new general theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain joint NL/Lean embeddings, retrieval-augmented formalization, verifier-guided repair, and the same two curated datasets. The abstract and conclusion retain the same scientific scope and headline performance claims. Expanded comparator coverage supplies additional support rather than redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving coarse domain clustering in text encoders, reduced tactic diversity under text retrieval, and cascading errors in the two-step pipeline. It interprets domain-level weaknesses and the appendix example's semantic mismatch. Appendix A.3 also introduces SC's flexibility-versus-reproducibility tradeoff with BEq+ and explicitly characterizes SC as conservative. These substantially expand the paper's scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: V1's appendix provides hardware/software information but few training settings. V2 Appendix A.2 specifies trainable encoder layers, dropout, token limits, optimizer, learning rates, batches, epochs, gradient accumulation/checkpointing, BF16, scheduling, and baseline decoding temperature/top-p. Sections 5.4–5.6 additionally disclose domain stratification and retrieval conditioning for the SFT-only variant. These materially improve implementation documentation without establishing changes to the underlying training.

R1.justification: V2 expands retrieval positioning beyond TLAPS/COPRA to REAL-Prover, LeanSearch, and RAutoformalizer, emphasizing theorem-proof structure versus plain-text retrieval. Appendix A.3 newly compares SC with BEq and BEq+, including their tactic restrictions and computational tradeoffs. New embedding-model and Gemini references further broaden the literature coverage.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and most method text remain stable. V2 revises the opening motivation and experimental discussion, separates metrics, baselines, setup, results, and ablations into individual subsections, and moves the existing semantic-equivalence appendix from A.2 to A.3. These are localized language and organizational refinements.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains encoder groups, parameter counts, and an mMG column. Table 2 moves to a separate page and introduces a setting column with grouped comparisons. V2 also adds Figure 3's stacked domain-performance bars and extensive boxed Lean listings in Appendix A.4. These substantially expand and restructure the empirical and appendix displays.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through larger retrieval baselines and a directly relevant two-step comparison, while Appendix A.2 supplies essential reproducibility details missing from v1. The net gain is limited by the unexplained three-to-five-example revision with retained scores, new prose–Table 2 discrepancies, and Appendix A.4's use of simp with arguments despite Appendix A.3's prohibition. The additions make the paper more informative, but its expanded validation remains internally inconsistent.
